learning.title: A person's explicit resume of an authority suspension lasts only until the next recheck (decision D1)
learning.trigger: Adding or changing an operation that resumes a request suspended for an authority reason (principal_inactive, actor_not_allowlisted, actor_role_insufficient, no_delegation, actor_unverifiable).
learning.mistake: Expecting a person's explicit resume (ticketRequests.create) to re-assign the request's recorded principal, origin or authority evidence, or to outlast the next recheck. The request keeps all three: they have no update grant (0145_ticket_admission.sql:290-294) and no operation re-assigns them. The next poll or webhook recheck judges the recorded principal again through recordedContext and suspends the request for the same reason.
learning.rule: The explicit call judges the caller's authority only. The request keeps its recorded principal, origin and authority evidence, so the call cannot hand the request to the caller.

The resume lasts until the next recheck and fails closed: no automatic run starts while the recorded authority is not live. A request without a run returns to waiting with a null reason; a request that owns a run becomes admitted or active and no run is started. The next recheck suspends it again, and pauses its run when the run has a live attempt on a worker whose adapter supports pause.

Recovery is to restore the recorded authority: the recorded principal's membership and a role with task:write and run:write, or the allowlist entry or role the recorded actor needs. The next recheck then resumes the request with no explicit call.

A changed delegation.principalId on the source does not reach an existing request, because recordedContext judges authority_principal_id. A changed allowlist, or a delegation set again after no_delegation, does reach it, because the policy is read live.

To release a ticket whose recorded principal is gone for good, the request must end: its run ends (runs.control cancel makes the run and its task canceled) or, with no finished run, its task is completed, failed or canceled (terminalOutcome). The next recheck then records the terminal disposition and frees the slot; until then the nonterminal request blocks the ticket through ticket_requests_one_nonterminal_idx. After it has ended, the next poll admits a new generation only if the source's delegation principal is live, because a new admission judges the source's principal, not the recorded one.

verification.requirement: The per-reason pins in tests/helpers/ticket-admission/resume-integration.ts cover each of the five reasons: the request is suspended, resumed by the explicit call, rechecked and suspended again for the same reason, with nothing started; restoring the authority then resumes it with no call.

learning.boundary: This release has no operation that cancels a task that has no run (tasks.update changes title, description, priority and planning-only only), so for such a request restoring the recorded principal is the supported exit.
